6XOY VB4->VCP.final: The indole C2 packing GLU109.O at 3.52 A becomes an oxindole carbonyl carbon whose new oxygen grows toward HIS115, while the ring NH's 2.85 A hydrogen bond to GLU109.OE2 is retained.
6XOY VB4->VCP.why: A adopted as written. Both numbers are input-table values (C18/GLU109.O 3.52; N19/GLU109.OE2 2.85, H-bond good geometry, also conserved 2.85->2.96 so 'retained' is permitted by rule 5). HIS115 has no atom-table row and I confirmed it in the <=4.5 A envelope band, so naming it is correct under rule 1; the sentence says 'grows toward' and asserts no contact, and no band is quoted. No room claim despite room_contradicts_edit. STEREO C15 R->S left undisclosed - acceptable at 31 words.
6XOY VB4->VCP.disagreement: All three named HIS115 from the envelope and all three used it as direction only. A alone kept the retained GLU109.OE2 hydrogen bond with its measured distance; B's 'turning that ring edge polar' and C's 'directing new polarity' are vaguer about the same carbonyl. A right.

6LYA EXL->ALN.final: Swapping the N-methylindole for a naphthalene gives up the N-methyl's 3.70 A packing on PHE347.O and the ring nitrogen's 3.66 A packing on ALA420.O, placing carbon toward LEU305 instead.
6LYA EXL->ALN.why: A adopted. C01 (CHANGED) faces PHE347.O 3.70 and N02 (CHANGED) faces ALA420.O 3.66, both polar/apolar packing, both described as packing per rule 9b. LEU305 is absent from the atom table and I confirmed it in the <=4.5 A envelope band, so the name is legal; direction only, no band cited. All three correctly refused the O/MET344.SD row ([INCOMPAT] and [CLOSE 2.43/3.3 uncertain]).
6LYA EXL->ALN.disagreement: Identical anchors in all three. C added 'trading polar packing for expected hydrophobic contact', a chemical expectation rather than an observation; B is nearly identical to A but longer. A is tightest and names both lost packing contacts with their own distances.

7XXP OI9->I60.final: Truncating the side chain deletes the nitrogen hydrogen-bonded to ASN299.O at 3.24 A, giving up that contact, while the sugar hydroxyl's 2.63 A hydrogen bond to THR466.OG1 is retained.
7XXP OI9->I60.why: A adopted. N14 (CHANGED) faces ASN299.O at 3.24 A, 103 deg, typed H-bond good geometry, so rule 2 licenses the term from an input row; the retained contact is the O03/a:O2 THR466.OG1 conserved row (2.63 input side cited, analogue side not). A names the nitrogen by what it does rather than asserting which nitrogen it is, which is right given the ring relabelling between the two SMILES. All three correctly refused the N12/GLU312 polar-contact-to-SALT-BRIDGE flip ([ANGLE-ONLY], contact lengthens - rule 10). No envelope residue needed.
7XXP OI9->I60.disagreement: B pointed the shortened chain at CYS281 (envelope 4.5-6.0) and C at CYS302 (envelope <=4.5); both are legal names but a deletion has no growth direction to assign, and the two picked different residues for the same retreat, which is itself a sign the direction is not readable. C also wrote a blanket 'GLU312 and ARG306 contacts held' when one GLU312 row is TYPING CHANGED. A, which claimed no direction, was right.

6VH0 QZD->QZ4.final: Two sites change: the isobutyl carbons packing GLN192.OE1 at 3.81 A and GLN192.CG at 3.72 A become a cyclohexyl reaching toward HIS41, and the dioxane becomes difluorocyclohexyl; the 1.82 A CYS148 covalent bond holds.
6VH0 QZD->QZ4.why: A adopted. C05/GLN192.OE1 3.81 and C06/GLN192.CG 3.72 are both input rows and both ATTACHMENT POINTs; the covalent claim rests on the input row C19 COVALENT BOND to CYS148.SG 1.82 A, measured on both sides (1.82->1.80), so rules 3 and 5 hold. TWO TRANSFORMATIONS is disclosed explicitly with the second group named chemically, which is the fullest rule-11 compliance of the three. HIS41 is envelope-only and I confirmed it in the <=4.5 A band; 'reaching toward' is the brief's expectation vocabulary, not a contact claim.
6VH0 QZD->QZ4.disagreement: B and C both named HIS41 and LEU49 (both envelope-only, both confirmed in the <=4.5 A band) where A named only HIS41; B's second-site disclosure is the bare 'the carbamate cap also changes'. C flagged honestly that the envelope cannot say which of the two transformations grows toward HIS41/LEU49. A wins on disclosure, B on direction; neither is wrong.

6VH1 QZ7->QZ4.final: The isobutyl methyl sitting against LEU49.CD2 at 3.70 A becomes a cyclohexyl, which should spread that packing over more ring carbons and extend toward HIS41, while the 1.81 A CYS148 covalent bond holds.
6VH1 QZ7->QZ4.why: A adopted - the cleanest two-half shape in the batch. C14 (CHANGED) faces LEU49.CD2 3.70 A hydrophobic, worded 'sitting against' per rule 9b; the consequence half is direction and kind with no magnitude; the covalent anchor is the input C25 row (1.81 A) confirmed conserved at 1.80. HIS41 is envelope-only, confirmed in the <=4.5 A band, used as direction. Single-site edit, so no rule-11 burden.
6VH1 QZ7->QZ4.disagreement: B used no envelope residue at all here, anchoring on GLN192.OE1 3.53 and LEU49.CD2 3.70 - both measured - and noted this pair as the control: LEU49 is atom-table here and envelope-only in 6VH0, the same destination from two inputs. That cross-check is the strongest evidence in the batch that the envelope is recovering real site residues. A and C added HIS41 on top; all three are defensible, A reads best.

8KE3 FXC->6CV.final: Replacing the trifluoromethyl, whose fluorines pack TRP417.CZ3 at 3.24-3.66 A and GLN348.NE2 at 3.78 A, with one bromine collapses that three-point packing onto a single halogen pointing toward GLY419.
8KE3 FXC->6CV.why: A adopted. Every number is an input row (F12 3.24 and F10 3.66 to TRP417.CZ3; F11 3.78 to GLN348.NE2) and the range is two input values, not an analogue measurement. All four CF3 atoms are CHANGED, so the loss is real. 'pack' only, per rule 9b. GLY419 is envelope-only, confirmed in the <=4.5 A band, and is given as a direction with no contact asserted. Only two conserved rows survive, so all three correctly avoided any 'retained' claim.
8KE3 FXC->6CV.disagreement: C deliberately named no envelope residue, arguing a CF3-to-Br swap at the same ring position predicts no new partner - a fair position, and the mirror of its own choice on 8KE6. B and A both pointed at GLY419. Since the analogue's bromine does face GLY419.O, the direction is defensible; A's phrasing collapses three contacts onto one atom, which is the real consequence.

8KE5 FXL->FXF.final: The aryl chlorine's 3.74 A hydrophobic packing on ALA302.CB is replaced by a larger, more polarisable bromine, which should tighten packing against that alanine face and the neighbouring GLN348 wall.
8KE5 FXL->FXF.why: C adopted over A and B. All three anchored correctly on CL1/ALA302.CB 3.74 A hydrophobic (CHANGED), but A and B then sent the bromine 'toward GLY401', a residue in the 4.5-6.0 envelope band. That name is legal and the analogue's Br does face GLY401.N, but a same-position Cl-to-Br swap gives no input-side reason to predict a new partner nearly 5 A away, so it is a direction the model would have to invent. C's GLN348 comes from the measured CE1 row (3.83 A, SUBSTITUTION BOUNDARY), so both halves stay on input evidence. No H-bond claimed on the [INCOMPAT] N row.
8KE5 FXL->FXF.disagreement: The split was exactly about envelope discipline: A and B used GLY401 from the 4.5-6.0 band and both flagged it in their own concerns as their weakest envelope use; C refused it as 'envelope-laundered guessing'. C was right - not because the name is forbidden, but because nothing on the input side predicts that direction.

8KE6 FCL->FXC.final: The chlorine packing GLY419.O at 3.18 A gives way to a trifluoromethyl at the ring carbon 3.68 A from ALA420.N, spreading three fluorines toward TRP417 instead of one halogen.
8KE6 FCL->FXC.why: A adopted. CL1 (CHANGED) faces GLY419.O 3.18 and CE1 (ATTACHMENT POINT) faces ALA420.N 3.68, both input rows, both worded as packing per rule 9b. TRP417 has no row in this input's atom table and I confirmed it in the <=4.5 A envelope band - this is the pair where the envelope was load-bearing: without it the CF3's destination had no nameable partner. Direction only, no band quoted, no contact asserted. The ring-position relabelling between the two namespaces is handled by describing groups, not atom names (rule 11).
8KE6 FCL->FXC.disagreement: All three named TRP417 from the envelope, and all three noted it is measured in 8KE3 (the reverse direction on the same ligand pair), which independently corroborates it as a real site residue. C went furthest with 'new fluorine contacts expected there' - an expected contact at an envelope-only residue, the one clause in the batch that leans on the envelope harder than it supports. A and B kept it directional; A right.

8GF0 UM9->ZHE.final: The gem-dimethyl ketone arm, whose carbons pack GLN389.O at 3.41-3.73 A while its ketone oxygen makes no contact in this crystal, becomes a cyclohexyl that should pack that face and grow toward ARG392.

C11 3.41 and C10 3.73 to GLN389.O are input rows and both CHANGED; O7, the ketone oxygen, is in the 'NOTHING WITHIN 4.0 A (listed, so the table is complete)' line, which rule 4 permits as a measurement. C is more precise than A, which called the replacement a cyclohexylmethyl when the OCH2 (C9) is kept as a SUBSTITUTION BOUNDARY - the arm becomes a cyclohexyl, not a cyclohexylmethyl. ARG392 is envelope-only, confirmed in the <=4.5 A band, given as direction only. No size language, correctly, since heavy-atom count is unchanged.

6YKK OVK->OVH.final: Three changes - ring expansion, a longer linker, a reconnected azole - relocate the nitrogen packing HIS52.NE2 at 3.95 A and shift the phenyl toward GLN580; the 2.80 A PHE41.O hydrogen bond is held.
6YKK OVK->OVH.why: Rewritten from A and C. The edit is genuinely three changes (furanose expanded to a six-membered ring, linker lengthened by one carbon, tetrazole reconnected as a triazole) with no TWO TRANSFORMATIONS flag to force disclosure, so rule 11 is satisfied explicitly. The anchor is moved onto N8, the atom site_of_change actually marks MOVED and which faces HIS52.NE2 at 3.95 A, rather than onto N10, which is CHANGED and therefore absent from the analogue - C described a deleted atom as moving. The retained 2.80 A PHE41.O hydrogen bond is a conserved row measured on both sides (2.80->2.80), permitted by rule 5. GLN580 is envelope-only, confirmed in the <=4.5 A band, used as a direction for the phenyl; no band cited.
6YKK OVK->OVH.disagreement: A said 'edited in three places' but named only two, and anchored on N8 (correctly MOVED). B and C both kept the PHE41.O hydrogen bond but anchored the arm on N10, a CHANGED atom. A and C pointed the arm at GLN580, B at LYS634 - both envelope-only and both confirmed in the <=4.5 A band, and A admitted it could not choose between them. The rewrite takes A's atom, C's multi-site disclosure and B's retained hydrogen bond.
